notes:
Background: Sparkbrush builds a VS Code extension (Sparkbrush Copilot) used by internal and external developers for in-editor completions, refactors, and test generation. Primary differentiator is low-latency inline suggestions and context-aware streaming completions optimized for large codebases.

Key asks from last calls:
- Need median token latency < 80ms for inline suggestions at 16k context window; tail p95 < 200ms.
- Streaming API that emits incremental completion tokens to VS Code extension (WebSocket/HTTP2 preferred).
- Ability to pin model versions per release channel (stable/dev/experimental) and rollout with A/B traffic split.
- Auth: enterprise SSO (SAML), token scoping per extension install, token refresh flow for long-running sessions.
- Rate limits: per-user and per-org throttles + burst buckets, ability to map to freemium vs paid seats.
- Security: audit logs for API calls, optional KMS integration for model keys, retention controls for snippets and telemetry, residency for EU customers.

POC scope: integrate Redwood Hosted API into current extension, run 2-week POC with 40 internal devs + 200 beta users. Metrics to capture: cold-start latency, median per-token latency, p95, error rate, tokens-per-minute throughput per org. POC milestone: demo streaming UX + integration doc by week 1, perf report + SSO smoke test by week 3.

Customer quote / sticky note: "If we can get consistent sub-100ms suggestions in VS Code for our large monorepo, adoption will spike — latency is the UX." — Head of Platform (Ethan Park)

Integration concerns / technical notes (from SE call):
- Currently using a Node-based extension backend; prefers easy SDK (JS/TS) and WS streaming sample.
- Wants explicit guidance on token caching vs. request-level auth to avoid leaking seats.
- Prefers ability to route lower-priority completions to smaller, cheaper quantized models for non-privileged users.
- Needs example rollout policy: stable channel -> pinned model v1.2.3, experimental channel -> latest nightly with auto-fallback.

Commercial / pricing notes:
- Interested in a hybrid: hosted API for most customers + dedicated pools for enterprise accounts.
- Looking for clear per-seat pricing and a cap for freemium usage to avoid bill surprises during beta.

Short-term next steps (CRM shorthand):
- Send POC checklist + integration SDK links (AE).
- SE to provide streaming sample repo + SLO test harness (Marcus).
- Security to review Redwood security FAQ + send SAML SP metadata (Nadia).

Requested artifacts (already linked): pricing deck, security questionnaire.

Potential upsell: Dedicated pools + extended log retention for enterprise customers (compliance).
